question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births registered in Taiwan in September 2026, as reported in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics.

target.what: Number of live births registered (出生登記) in Taiwan during September 2026, as published in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics (戶口統計 / 人口統計月報), national total (all counties/cities), counted by registration date (登記日期) rather than by date of occurrence
target.publisher: Ministry of the Interior, Department of Household Registration (內政部戶政司) — monthly household registration / population statistics bulletin, typically released around the 8th–10th of the following month
target.caveats: The target period is FUTURE and incomplete at the 2026-09-08 cutoff: this is a forecast, and the figure will normally only be published in early-to-mid October 2026, so no observation of the target itself can exist. Definitional issues that materially change the number: (a) MOI's headline monthly 'b

candidates.hypothesis: Monthly registered births have a fairly stable within-year seasonal shape plus a declining trend, so September 2026 can be anchored either by September 2025 scaled by the recent year-on-year ratio, or by the 2026 year-to-date monthly average scaled by the historical September seasonal index. The relationship is direct (same definition, same publisher) and needs only a stable-shape assumption.
candidates.data_to_find: MOI monthly national birth registration counts (出生人數) for every month from 2019-01 through the latest month published before 2026-09-08 (ideally July or August 2026); specifically the September values 2019–2025 and all 2026 months available. Minimum evidence: at least 5 September observations plus 2026 Jan–Jul monthly values. Substitute: annual totals plus monthly shares if monthly detail is unavailable.

candidates.perspective: household registration office processing birth registrations
candidates.hypothesis: Registered births in month m = births occurring in m that are registered within m + late registrations of births from m-1 and earlier. The lag distribution is administratively determined (60-day legal window), so a stable same-month registration share lets us convert an occurrence-based forecast into a registration-based one, or calibrate a registration-only trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Distribution of registration lag, or cross-tabulations of 出生 by 發生日期 vs 登記日期 for recent months (share of a month's occurrences registered in the same calendar month, next month, later); any statement of average days from birth to registration in Taiwan. Minimum evidence: same-month share for a few recent months, or monthly 出生通報 vs 出生登記 totals for overlapping months.

candidates.perspective: health ministry birth-notification system and hospitals
candidates.hypothesis: Births notified by hospitals (出生通報) approximate all live births by occurrence date with near-complete coverage, so the ratio 出生登記/出生通報 is a stable bridge factor; the notification series also gives a faster, higher-frequency read on recent birth levels (through mid-2026) that feeds the September forecast via trend and seasonality.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly 出生通報 counts (by month of birth) from 衛福部國民健康署 / 出生通報統計 for 2023–2026 (latest available before cutoff), matching MOI monthly registered births for the same months so a ratio can be derived. Substitute: 出生數 by 發生日期 from MOI.

candidates.hypothesis: Births in month m correspond to first-trimester prenatal visits roughly 7–9 months earlier; NHI-reimbursed prenatal checkup volumes (or first-visit counts) for late 2025 and early 2026 therefore constrain September–October 2026 births. The bridge is a lead-time/coverage factor, assuming prenatal-care uptake and visit schedules stay stable.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly NHI prenatal checkup claim counts (產前檢查 申報件數/人次) and, if available, first-visit or 妊娠週數-specific counts, from 健保署 open data or 國健署 孕婦產檢 utilization statistics, 2023–2026. Minimum evidence: monthly totals through at least early 2026 plus a rough lead-time distribution.

candidates.perspective: demographers linking marriage and first births
candidates.hypothesis: In Taiwan a large share of births occur within roughly 1–2 years of marriage registration, and monthly marriages lead monthly births by about 10–15 months; marriage registrations in mid-2025 therefore carry information about September 2026 births, and the marriage series helps explain deviations from the pure seasonal extrapolation.
candidates.data_to_find: MOI monthly marriage registration counts (結婚對數) 2023-01 to the latest month before cutoff, plus (if available) the distribution of interval from marriage to first birth in Taiwan. Minimum evidence: monthly marriage series covering mid-2024 to mid-2025 and a parity-specific or first-birth interval estimate.

candidates.perspective: social insurance and municipal birth-bonus administrators
candidates.hypothesis: Maternity benefit claims (勞保/國保/農保 生育給付) and municipal birth-bonus applications are filed shortly after birth and cover a large, stable share of all births, so their monthly counts act as an early proxy with a short lag and can validate the level implied by registration-based routes.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly 勞保生育給付 件數 (and 國保/農保 if available) from 勞動部勞工保險局 statistical reports, 2024–2026; any published ratio of claim counts to total births; municipal 生育獎勵金 application counts if released monthly.

candidates.hypothesis: September births equal the 2026 annual birth total multiplied by September's share of annual births (historically a fairly narrow band). Full-year 2026 forecasts or targets from 國發會/內政部 projections and mid-year media or expert forecasts therefore give an independent level anchor, cross-checking d1.
candidates.data_to_find: Any 2026 full-year birth forecast, projection or target published on or before 2026-09-08 (國發會 人口推估, 內政部 statements, academic or media estimates based on H1 2026 data), plus the historical September share of annual births computed from MOI annual and monthly series (2015–2025).

candidates.hypothesis: Zodiac-year effects (2024 dragon peak, 2025 snake trough, 2026 horse year), the timing of Lunar New Year (2026-02-17) shifting conceptions, and any 2025–2026 birth-incentive policy changes can shift the September 2026 level and the year-on-year ratio relative to a naive seasonal extrapolation; quantifying the zodiac and LNY effects from history converts them into an adjustment multiplier.
candidates.data_to_find: Annual (and where possible monthly) Taiwan birth counts by zodiac year 1990–2025 to estimate the horse-year/snake-year/dragon-year multipliers; documentation of Lunar New Year dates and any observed conception-month dips; announcements before 2026-09-08 of new birth subsidies, 婚育 policies, or marriage/birth incentive changes effective in 2025–2026.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
